why_trail.why: Handoff is complete and internally consistent; no blocker. The load-bearing constraint is confirmed by reading the source: advance's require_why comes from _run_verb's live _trip_hard_band_reading call at checklist_engine.py:3369, not from any caller flag, and at/over hard it refuses --mechanical outright (:2524-2532). Also found, and it changes the fixture design: start (not advance) is TRIP_HARD_GUARDED (:83, dispatch :3333), so a hard-band fixture whose gate is still pending would be refused at start with the begin-refused message instead of reaching the why-required refusal -- the HARD-band fixture's gate must therefore already be in-progress. For the gauge to be read at all, the fixture needs an ACTIVE lease (_checklist_owner keys the filename off it), observed_at at/after claimed_at (_reading_predates_claim), a model in gauge_reader._PROFILES, and freshness within 30 minutes.

done_refusal lands beside the pure helpers with the two new checks in the handoff's exact order and wording, then delegates to closeout_refusal. Two judgment calls, both toward failing visibly: archive_exists is a REQUIRED keyword (a default could only be False, the permissive answer, so a forgotten argument would silently skip the archive check -- and closeout_refusal's own archive_exists is required for the same reason); and the delegation is pinned by a parametrized differential test over all six of closeout_refusal's outcomes including None, plus a source assertion that the body neither restates engine_session/_TERMINAL_STATUSES/consolidation nor adds a second archive check. 15 new tests green.

_engine_call lands as the module's one engine choke point, mirroring mcp_spine_server.run_engine: one io.StringIO behind redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr, checklist_engine.main(argv), return (text, code). Four clauses, ordered SystemExit (a BaseException, so no except Exception can stand in for it) then EngineError then a broad Exception -- the broad one is load-bearing, not tidiness, because main() does parse_args and load() BEFORE its own EngineError handler, so a missing or unparseable spine file raises OSError/ValueError straight past every engine-side guard. Two tests had to change shape: the one-choke-point assertion is measured over the AST, not by text search, because the module and the function both DISCUSS checklist_engine.main in prose and prose is not a call site. Also recorded: an external actor reset this worktree to HEAD mid-gate and destroyed the m1 edits (reflog: 'reset: moving to HEAD'); re-applied, and both files are now backed up outside the worktree after every green step. 25 tests green.

_advance_and_release drives start (only when pending) then advance then release through _engine_call, and returns a refusal verbatim with the stage that produced it. The byte-identity assertion is measured against a SEPARATE PROCESS running the real CLI over the same argv on an identical pristine copy of the fixture, so 'verbatim' is pinned to the engine itself rather than to a second call into the same helper. A spy on _engine_call proves exactly one engine call happens on a refused advance -- no silent retry with a different flag, no release. One test had to be reshaped: a non-owner session is refused by require_session at the ADVANCE, so stage 'release' needs an already-terminal spine where the advance half is skipped; both cases are now pinned separately. 12 tests green.

The HARD-band refusal is reproduced in a tmp_path fixture, not argued for. Six tests: a negative control that asserts the gauge is genuinely over the line (gauge_reader.read returns a Reading, fill >= thresholds_for's hard, and checklist_engine._trip_hard_band_reading agrees on this exact spine); the why-less close refused with the engine's own wording and NOTHING recorded on the why_trail; byte-identity against the real CLI in a separate process on a pristine copy carrying its own gauge; THE SAME fixture closing cleanly once a why is supplied, with the understanding landing on the why_trail; the innocent counterpart below the line where --mechanical still succeeds, which proves the band and not the fixture causes the refusal; and a spy proving exactly one engine call and no release after the refusal. Four fixture conditions were load-bearing and none of them are guessable from the handoff: an ACTIVE lease (it keys the gauge filename), observed_at not before claimed_at, a model in _PROFILES, and freshness under 30 minutes -- plus the gate having to be in-progress rather than pending, because start and not advance is TRIP_HARD_GUARDED.
